name: Bearish Seagull Spread
summary: Buy a put spread financed by selling an OTM call; the bearish mirror of the seagull, with uncovered upside risk.

legs.strike_rule: call delta 0.15-0.25, at or above resistance (UNCOVERED)
ATM or slightly OTM, put delta -0.45 to -0.55
put delta -0.20 to -0.25, at the downside target

when_to_use: COMPLETENESS / LEVEL 4: the short call is uncovered. Under Level 3, replace the naked short call with a call credit spread (which makes it an unbalanced iron condor) or simply trade the put debit spread alone.
max_profit: (long put strike - short put strike) x 100 + net credit
max_loss: UNDEFINED above the short call strike
breakevens: downside breakeven = long put strike - debit/100; upside breakeven = short call strike + credit/100
entry_rules: BLOCKED AT LEVEL 3: uncovered short call requires Alpaca level 4; the router must reject this slug.
Level 4 version: short call delta <= 0.25 and above a 60-session resistance level; target near-zero net cost.
Level-3 substitute: buy a call above the short call, converting the financing leg into a call credit spread.
management_rules: Level 4 only: close at 65% of the put spread's max value.
Level 4 only: close at 21 DTE, or immediately if the short call delta reaches 0.45.
exit_rules: ASSIGNMENT GUARD: uncovered short call; flatten by 15:45 ET on expiration day, unconditionally.
ASSIGNMENT GUARD: close the short call immediately if ITM with extrinsic < $0.10.
DIVIDEND GUARD: close the short call before every ex-dividend date when it is ITM.
assignment_risk: Uncovered short call assignment creates a naked short stock position with unbounded risk and an immediate margin call on a $50k account.
buying_power: Naked short call margin plus the put spread debit.
common_mistakes: Attempting it at Level 3; assuming the long put hedges the short call (it does not).
family: three-leg-structures (butterflies, broken-wing butterflies, lizards, three-strike ratio spreads, ladders/tree spreads, christmas trees, and three-leg stock+option hybrids)
blocked_because: needs Alpaca options level 4; this account is level 3. Alpaca rejects it with 'account not eligible to trade uncovered option contracts'. Raising the level is an Alpaca approval, not a code change.
